Distributed optimal control

Source: R/inverse-problems.R
optimal_control.Rd

Solves the linear-quadratic optimal control problem

Usage

optimal_control(
  mesh,
  target,
  alpha,
  diffusion = 1,
  source = 0,
  bcs = dirichlet_bc(0),
  lower = NULL,
  upper = NULL,
  control = list()
)

Arguments

mesh

A pde_mesh().

target

Desired state u_target(x, y).

alpha

Control cost (positive).

diffusion

Diffusion coefficient.

source

Fixed source f.

bcs

Boundary conditions of the state equation.

lower, upper

Optional control bounds (numbers).

control

Passed to stats::optim().

Value

A list of class pde_control with the control and state functions, the objective, the gradient norm and solver details.

Details

min_q 1/2 ||u - u_target||^2 + alpha/2 ||q||^2

subject to -div(k grad u) = f + q with the given boundary conditions, where the control q is a P1 function and norms are L2 norms (computed with the mass matrix). The problem is strictly convex for alpha > 0.

Without bounds the first-order optimality (KKT) system is solved directly with sparse LU. With bounds lower <= q <= upper, the reduced problem is solved with stats::optim() ("L-BFGS-B") using adjoint gradients and a single Cholesky factorization of the state operator.

Examples

mesh <- pde_mesh_rectangle(nx = 8)
oc <- optimal_control(mesh, target = function(x, y) sin(pi * x) * sin(pi * y),
                      alpha = 1e-4)
oc
#> Distributed optimal control (KKT (sparse LU))
#>   objective 0.00479426, projected gradient norm 3.76e-17
#>   control range [-2.025e-11, 19.68]
